subject: Mutual action plan: hosting lane and region constraints (MedNova)
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Ami Patel <ami.patel@mednova.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual action plan kickoff — hosting lane & region asks

Hi Ami — great to meet you on the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, attaching an initial MAP and a short hosting cost summary so your engineering and compliance teams can line up questions. High level asks from our side to help accelerate evaluation: 

- Primary decision points for MedNova: Hosted (fastest), Dedicated (reserved capacity + isolation), Private (on-prem / VPC). Which lane do you want us to prioritize in the MAP?
- Region requirement / data residency: do you need strict US-only (us-east/us-west) or any chance for EU (eu-west) in scope?
- Timeline: recommend SOW signature (2 weeks), pilot (4–6 weeks), production ramp (target 8–12 weeks after pilot).

Please review the MAP_v1.xlsx and the hosting-cost-estimates.pdf (attached). If you can confirm procurement and security contacts, we’ll add them to the MAP and propose specific milestone dates.

Next steps I suggest:
1) You confirm hosting lane preference and residency constraints this week.
2) We schedule a 30-min sync (engineering + security) early next week to review the SOC2 evidence and data flow.

Thanks — happy to adjust cadence to your calendar.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
attachments: MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), hosting-cost-estimates.pdf (pdf)

From: Ami Patel <ami.patel@mednova.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@mednova.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan kickoff — hosting lane & region asks

Kimberly — thanks, and thanks again for the demo. A few clarifying Qs from our side: 

- Data residency: MedNova must ensure PHI stays within US boundaries for this initial pilot. Can Hosted guarantee that? If not, we need an approach that gives us contractual and technical controls.
- Encryption + KMS: we need customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) for the production lane — is that supported on Dedicated/Private?
- Compliance pack: please include any SOC2 excerpts and penetration test summaries in the next drop.

Looping procurement for SOW cadence.

Ami
Ami Patel
Head of Digital Products, MedNova Health
ami.patel@mednova.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Ami Patel <ami.patel@mednova.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan kickoff — hosting lane & region asks

Ami — quick answers inline and a link to the security excerpts: 

- Hosted + US-only: we can route all tenant traffic to US regions (us-east or us-west) and enforce contractually that no processing occurs outside selected regions. For extra assurance we can add contractual residency language and an attestation schedule.
- Dedicated: customer gets reserved GPU pools in the chosen region; supports customer-managed KMS (via our KMS integrations and optional HSM connector).
- Private: full VPC/on-prem option for air-gapped or regulated workflows.

I’m attaching SOC2_summary.pdf for your security team to review. Also see: https://app.redwood.com/docs/hosting-runtimes#hosted-vs-dedicated for a short comparison table.

If US-only residency is a hard requirement for pilot, our recommended path to accelerate timeto-value is: start Hosted in a US region with residency language + DPA, then move to Dedicated if/when you need reserved capacity or stricter KMS control. That path keeps time-to-first-API low while addressing procurement concerns.

Would you and procurement be available for a joint 45-minute call on Friday to agree the SOW milestones?

Kim
attachments: SOC2_summary.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Mutual action plan kickoff — hosting lane & region asks

Kim — quick internal note (forwarding my thoughts to keep on record):

On the Hosted-first approach: I agree with the ramp strategy but recommend we build two explicit fallback gates into the MAP:

- Gate A (Proof-of-concept acceptance): If performance and latency targets are met in us-east Hosted for 2 weeks, we auto-escalate to Pilot. If not, we propose Dedicated in us-east within 10 business days.
- Gate B (Security/KMS): If procurement requires customer-managed keys before Pilot, treat Dedicated as default and flag Private as last-resort.

Also propose we include an explicit rollback/fallback policy (nightly cache purge, KV-sync notes) to reassure their SREs.

—Marcus
